# Halcyon Threshold — Emberfall Rapid Grant Proposal

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale  
**Project:** Independent evaluation of frontier-model incident-response readiness  
**Amount requested:** $7,500 USD  
**Duration:** 3 months (December 2026 – February 2027), evenings and weekends  
**Status:** Draft — pending Morgan's review

---

## 1. What I'll do

I will run a small, independent evaluation project assessing whether frontier AI labs have published, verifiable incident-response plans for serious safety incidents (e.g., model escape, unauthorized exfiltration, self-replication attempts). Most public discussion focuses on pre-deployment evals; far less attention is paid to what happens *after* a incident is detected — who is notified, what containment steps exist, whether drills are run, and whether plans are tested externally.

Deliverables:
1. A survey of the top 10 frontier-model developers, reviewing public statements, job postings, and any published incident-response documentation.
2. A short report scoring each lab on transparency, verifiability, and external accountability of incident-response plans.
3. A template incident-response playbook that independent researchers and smaller labs could adopt.
4. All findings published under the Halcyon Threshold name (not my personal name), consistent with my employment constraints.

## 2. Why me

I founded Halcyon Threshold specifically to work on neglected AI-safety questions. I have decent writing skills, okay Python (for scraping/public-record review), and evenings/weekends to commit. I am not affiliated with a lab, so I can evaluate without conflicts of interest. I was referred to Emberfall by Idris Bellamy (program officer) after meeting at the November meetup.

I am currently employed at Dorrance Logistics and have not yet cleared public statements with HR. All public output will be under the Halcyon Threshold organization name, not my personal name, until HR clearance is obtained.

## 3. What it costs

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Domain renewal (halcyonthreshold.org, 1 year) | $15 |
| Pagewell Pro hosting (custom domain, 3 months @ $20/mo) | $60 |
| Compute / API costs for evaluation tooling | $200 |
| Stipend for ~40 hours of evenings/weekends over 3 months | $7,225 |
| **Total** | **$7,500** |

I am also contributing up to $2,000 of personal savings this year to Halcyon Threshold regardless of this grant.

---

*This draft is in the repo at proposals/emberfall-rapid-grant.md. I will submit the application once you confirm.*

# Halcyon Threshold

**Mission:** Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## About

Halcyon Threshold is an independent effort founded by Morgan Hale. We believe the arrival of superintelligence is the most important event of our lifetime, and almost nobody we know is working on it. We'd rather try and fail than watch.

## Current Work

We are running an independent evaluation of frontier-model incident-response readiness — surveying whether the leading AI developers have published, verifiable plans for serious safety incidents (model escape, unauthorized exfiltration, self-replication attempts). Most attention goes to pre-deployment evaluations; far less goes to what happens *after* an incident is detected.

## Contact

Email: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

---
*Started November 2026. Independent, self-funded, evenings and weekends.*
